b613d09f-d0c7-4e89-860a-573bccf8e069.content:
F5 complete: crates/zellij_host hosts each worker in a named pane of a
long-lived headless zellij session (REQ-1d).

Adapter surface:
- session_ensure(name) -> SessionHandle (idempotent; creates a detached
  background session so a human can `zellij attach` later to inspect)
- pane_create(session, name, command, env, cwd) -> PaneHandle
- pane_alive(pane) -> bool
- pane_close(pane)

Scope decision (recorded in REQ-1d): a feasibility spike of zellij 0.44.2's
library crates found a pure-library zellij_host is impractical -- zellij's
server must run as a daemonized process regardless of approach, zellij exposes
no per-pane environment API anywhere, and zellij-server/zellij-utils carry no
stability promise. zellij_host therefore drives the zellij CLI as a
subprocess: a deliberate, scoped exception to REQ-1a. The shell-out is
confined to one helper in this crate; the orchestrator core reaches zellij
only through this adapter. The xtask no-shell-out lint (AC-24) exempts
crates/zellij_host accordingly, and the design doc REQ-1d / REQ-1a were
amended to match.

Implementation notes:
- env has no zellij-native representation, so pane_create applies it by
  prefixing the command with `env KEY=VALUE ...`.
- panes are created with --close-on-exit, so pane_alive reports false once a
  worker's command exits; liveness is read from `zellij action list-panes
  --json`.
- ZellijError is a self-contained miette::Diagnostic (REQ-1b).

AC-27: tests/spawn.rs creates a real headless session, spawns a worker pane,
asserts it is alive while running and closes on exit, and verifies env
application via a marker file. Passes.

Delivered as 4 bisectable commits (design+lint amendment, skeleton+
session_ensure, pane operations, AC-27 test). Full workspace builds and
`just lint` is clean.

21785547-9460-4340-a552-cd8b4132f89c.title: Pin crosslink via npins instead of a Cargo.toml git dependency
21785547-9460-4340-a552-cd8b4132f89c.description:
## Context

crossbridge currently declares crosslink as a direct git dependency in its
workspace `Cargo.toml`:

    crosslink = { git = "https://github.com/forecast-bio/crosslink.git", rev = "12eb7b9..." }

vetinari (vringar/vetinari) pins crosslink differently. The approach makes nix
packaging cleaner and is a prerequisite for the two projects to interoperate (see
"Why this matters" below). Sharing the recipe.

## vetinari's approach

- **npins** pins crosslink in `npins/sources.json` (type Git, GitHub
  forecast-bio/crosslink, a branch plus a locked revision and tarball hash). Bump
  with `npins update crosslink`.
- **shell.nix** (plain nixpkgs, no flakes) exposes the pinned source as an env
  var: `CROSSLINK_SRC = "${sources.crosslink}"`.
- crosslink is **not on crates.io**, so a `[patch.crates-io]` cannot redirect it.
  Instead an insulation crate path-depends on a local copy of the source.
- A `just bootstrap` recipe (also run by the shell `shellHook`) copies
  `$CROSSLINK_SRC` into a **writable**, gitignored `.crosslink-src` tree. A
  symlink into the read-only nix store does NOT work: crosslink's `build.rs`
  writes a dashboard placeholder into the tree, and its server module embeds
  `dashboard/dist` via `rust-embed`, so bootstrap also `mkdir -p dashboard/dist`
  and writes a placeholder `index.html` so the derive compiles without a built
  frontend.
- The copy is guarded by a marker file holding the store path, so it only
  re-copies when the pin actually moves — avoiding mtime churn and needless
  rebuilds.

## Why this matters for crossbridge specifically

vetinari issue #25 integrates crossbridge by embedding `crossbridge-server` as a
library. That puts crossbridge's crosslink dependency and vetinari's own crosslink
dependency in one cargo dependency graph. `libsqlite3-sys` carries
`links = "sqlite3"`, which forces the *entire* graph to a single crosslink (and
single rusqlite) instance — two different crosslink revisions is a hard cargo
build failure, not a `[patch]`-able mismatch.

So crossbridge and vetinari must resolve crosslink to the **same commit**. Pinning
crosslink via npins (rather than a hard-coded `rev` in `Cargo.toml`) is what makes
that coordination tractable: the revision lives in one `npins/sources.json` entry,
and the nix dev shell provides a single crosslink source path that both projects
share.

Happy to share vetinari's exact `npins/sources.json` crosslink entry, `shell.nix`,
and `just bootstrap` recipe.

Filed from vetinari issue #25, architect finding B2.

e2dc2b35-fdb5-4dfc-8d9f-12a6bac42e06.author: desktop
e2dc2b35-fdb5-4dfc-8d9f-12a6bac42e06.content:
F6 complete (commit fc659542).

xtask gained a "lint" subcommand: the no-shell-out hard lint (AC-24). It
parses every orchestrator-side crate's src/ tree with syn and fails the
build on any Command::new() targeting jj, git, gh, crosslink, or zellij.

Design choices:
- syn AST parse, not text grep: banned names in comments, doc strings, or
  unrelated string literals never false-positive.
- Test code exempt: cfg(test) modules, test / tokio::test functions, and
  tests/ directories are pruned (the test harness legitimately drives the
  real CLIs, per AC-27).
- Scans all crates under crates/ automatically; escaping requires a
  deliberate xtask-only entry in EXEMPT_CRATES, so new orchestrator crates
  cannot silently bypass the audit.
- claude / claude-sandbox are simply not in the banned set (no library
  exists), so no separate exception list is needed.

Verification:
- 8 unit tests cover detection, every banned target, claude allowance,
  comment/string false-positive immunity, and all test-exemption paths.
- End-to-end: a planted Command::new("jj") in orchestrator/src made
  "just lint" exit 1 with a file:line:col report; removing it restored
  a clean pass.
- Full gate green: nix-shell just build / just test (12 tests) / just lint.

Known limitations (documented in lint.rs): a renamed import
(use Command as C) or a non-literal target (Command::new(&var)) is not
detected. The lint is a regression guardrail, not a sandbox.

5fd1c5d0-f1cd-4704-9732-1ae358da031a.title: crossbridge-server: run() needs a programmatic shutdown path for library embedders
5fd1c5d0-f1cd-4704-9732-1ae358da031a.description:
## Context

vetinari (an autonomous orchestrator — vringar/vetinari) wants to embed
`crossbridge-server` as a library, calling `crossbridge_server::run::run(ServerConfig)`
on its own runtime to act as an inbound crossbridge peer, rather than spawning the
`crossbridge-server` binary as a subprocess.

Two things in the current `run()` block clean library embedding.

## Problem

1. **No programmatic shutdown.** `run()`'s only non-error exit is `signal::ctrl_c()`.
   There is no `CancellationToken`, shutdown channel, or any parameter by which an
   embedder can ask the server loop to stop. An embedding host cannot cleanly bring
   the server down as part of its own shutdown.

2. **`process::exit(0)` inside `serve_one_session`.** On Ctrl-C the server calls
   `std::process::exit(0)` directly. Embedded in a host process this (a) bypasses
   every flush/checkpoint the host must perform before exiting, and (b) makes
   crossbridge's own `ctrl_c` handler race the host's signal handling — whichever
   fires first wins, and crossbridge's path terminates the whole process.

Together these force an embedder to reimplement `run()`'s loop (~50 lines, on top
of the `supervisor`/`listeners`/`handler` modules) just to obtain a shutdown
channel — duplicating upstream logic that will then drift.

## Request

- Add an optional shutdown signal to `run()` / `ServerConfig` — e.g. `run()` accepts
  a `tokio_util::sync::CancellationToken` (or a `tokio::sync::oneshot`/`watch`
  receiver). When triggered, the loop returns `Ok(())`.
- Remove the `process::exit(0)` in `serve_one_session`; return `Ok(())` from the
  loop and let the caller own process exit.
- Keep `ctrl_c` as the *binary's* behavior — `crossbridge-server/src/main.rs` can
  create a token and wire it to `signal::ctrl_c()` — but `run()` itself should not
  own signal handling or call `process::exit`.

This gives library embedders clean shutdown semantics and removes the need to fork
the run loop.

Filed from vetinari issue #25 (crossbridge integration), architect finding B1/B1a.

f8a8f1b4-93c2-4554-bd72-e0551e104a9d.author: desktop
f8a8f1b4-93c2-4554-bd72-e0551e104a9d.content:
F3 complete: crates/crosslink_api wraps the crosslink library crate behind a
stable adapter surface (REQ-3a).

CrosslinkRepo handle:
- discover() / open(repo_root) -- locate a .crosslink/ repository
- read_issue(id) -> IssueInfo (issue fields + labels)
- comment_write(id, kind, body, role_metadata) -> comment id
- label_add / label_remove(id, name) -> bool
- sign(payload, namespace) -> base64 signature
- key_ensure_loaded() -> fingerprint

Sourcing: crosslink is pinned via npins (forecast-bio/crosslink, develop
branch). It is not on crates.io and its build.rs writes a dashboard
placeholder into its own tree, so `just bootstrap` copies the npins-pinned
source to a writable .crosslink-src tree and crosslink_api path-depends on it.
.crosslink-src is excluded from the workspace so crosslink stays a plain
dependency. shell.nix exports CROSSLINK_SRC; bump via `npins update crosslink`.

Design notes:
- CrosslinkError is a self-contained miette::Diagnostic (REQ-1b). crosslink's
  library API is uniformly anyhow-based with no typed errors; the underlying
  cause is boxed so neither crosslink nor anyhow types leak into this crate's
  public signatures -- anyhow is not a dependency of this library crate.
- comment_write and the label operations branch on crosslink's SharedWriter:
  hub repositories route through it, single-agent repositories write the
  database directly -- mirroring crosslink's own CLI, since a direct write in
  hub mode is lost to the next hydration.
- key_ensure_loaded is verify-only: it never generates an identity, since
  provisioning a signing key is a deliberate crosslink setup step.
- crosslink's API is synchronous, so the adapter is too.

Tested: 6 integration tests build a throwaway crosslink repository and
round-trip issue reads, labels, comments, and the IssueNotFound /
NotARepository / IdentityUnavailable / InvalidCommentKind error paths. The
full workspace builds, `just lint` is clean (17 files scanned), and the whole
test suite passes.

Delivered as 3 commits: build wiring, adapter surface, integration test.

ac8126f8-d8d5-4d0d-b72b-7cfc6b0d47d7.title: vringar/crossbridge integration — research & decide scope
ac8126f8-d8d5-4d0d-b72b-7cfc6b0d47d7.description:
Question: 

Context: 

Findings: 

Research/decision issue — not yet designed. The integration scope is an open
question and is filed at critical priority so it gets resolved before any
implementation issues are broken out.

## What crossbridge is
vringar/crossbridge is a cross-repo IPC tool. Topology:
- `crossbridge-supervisor` runs on the host and owns `<root>/register.socket`.
- A per-repo `crossbridge-server --group <name> --slug <repo>` registers with it.
- `crossbridge-client {peers, submit, answer}` talks over the same `<root>`.

## Why this matters to vetinari (the open question)
Candidate roles — one must be chosen during the design pass:
1. Cross-instance coordination: multiple vetinari instances (one per project)
   share host-wide state through crossbridge.
2. Worker cross-repo Q&A: vetinari workers use peers/submit/answer to ask
   agents running in other repos mid-task.
3. Inbound submissions: the vetinari orchestrator registers a crossbridge
   server and answers submissions routed to it from other repos/agents.

## Hard constraint already known
crossbridge's socket root (`/run/crossbridge` or `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/crossbridge`)
is NOT bind-mounted into `claude-sandbox`. Any worker-side crossbridge use
(roles 2 and 3) requires the spawn helper (#8 / REQ-4) to bind the socket
directory or point `CROSSBRIDGE_SOCKET_ROOT` at an already-bound path.
Orchestrator-side use (role 1) runs outside the sandbox and is unaffected.

## Next steps
- [ ] Decide the integration role(s) above.
- [ ] If worker-side: design the sandbox socket-mount change against REQ-4 / #8.
- [ ] Run the-architect on the resulting design before breaking out impl issues.
- [ ] Integrate the decision into `.design/vdd-orchestrator.md` (or a new design doc).

## Known upstream papercuts (prior session)
From `.crosslink-bug-report.md` / knowledge page F0b: `crossbridge-client` should
suggest running the supervisor when no socket root exists; `--issue` should accept
the L-prefixed local form.

Stable adapter surface: workspace_add/forget/list, status, diff(rev_range) -> patch, log(revset), describe(rev, msg), bookmark_create/move/list, rebase(src_rev, dest_rev), git_push(remote, bookmark). ca5e58aa-4098-4bea-bc5b-475b0d0ec2b5.author: desktop
ca5e58aa-4098-4bea-bc5b-475b0d0ec2b5.content:
F4 complete: crates/jj_api now wraps jj-lib behind a stable adapter surface (REQ-1c).

JjWorkspace exposes the full operation set the issue calls for:
- workspace_add / workspace_forget / workspace_list
- status (read-only working-copy-vs-parent change list)
- diff(from, to) rendering a git-format patch
- log(revset)
- describe(revset, message)
- bookmark_create / bookmark_move / bookmark_list
- rebase(source, destination)
- git_push(remote, bookmark)

Design notes:
- JjError is a self-contained miette::Diagnostic enum; every variant boxes the
  underlying jj-lib cause, so jj-lib error types never leak into this crate's
  public signatures (REQ-1b). All jj-lib API churn is contained here.
- jj-lib is async-heavy; the adapter drives its futures on the current thread
  via pollster, keeping the public surface synchronous and pulling no tokio
  runtime into the orchestrator (REQ-1a).
- jj-lib is resolved from the nix-pinned jujutsu source via a generated
  .cargo/config.toml patch (REQ-1, REQ-1c).
- No std::process::Command anywhere in the crate; git_push relies on jj-lib
  running the git binary itself. The AC-24 no-shell-out lint passes (15 files
  scanned, clean).

AC-25: tests/lifecycle.rs drives add -> status -> diff -> describe -> list
(plus log, bookmarks, rebase) entirely through library calls and passes.

Delivered as 10 bisectable commits, one per operation group; the full
workspace builds and `just lint` is clean.

status is intentionally read-only (no working-copy snapshot): workers drive
the jj CLI which snapshots on every invocation, so the recorded working-copy
commit is current when the orchestrator inspects a workspace, and a read-only
status cannot corrupt a live worker workspace.
